tip: Informal commands to one person drop the pronoun and the -st ending: kommen becomes Komm.
Past passive uses wurde plus a participle: Der Vertrag wurde unterschrieben marks a completed past action.
Separable verbs slot ge- between prefix and stem in the participle: umbauen becomes umgebaut.
Verbs ending in -ieren form the participle with no ge-: operieren becomes operiert, not geoperiert.
Repeated time points use the accusative: jeden Freitag means every Friday, with jeden marking the case.
Days take am, a contraction of an dem: am Montag means on Monday.
For a fixed position, zwischen takes the dative: zwischen den Stalaktiten shows location, not movement across.
Comparisons use als for than after a comparative: älter als ich means older than I am.
denken pairs with an plus the accusative for to think of: denk an deinen Regenschirm.
Verbs that shift e to i keep it in the du-command: nehmen gives Nimm, not Nehm.
Formal commands keep Sie right after the verb: Erzählen Sie uns. The pronoun stays, unlike informal commands.
raten takes a dative person for to advise someone: ich rate dir means I advise you.
A present passive plus a future time word reads as future: wird nächste Woche repariert means will be repaired next week.
halb counts toward the next hour, not past the last: halb neun means 8:30, half an hour before nine.
sollen can mean supposed to or reportedly: es soll regnen means rain is expected, people say so.
In passives, name the doer with von plus dative: von vielen Leuten besucht means attended by many people.
The du-command of sein is irregular: it is simply Sei, as in Sei nicht traurig.
German keeps the present tense with seit for actions still going on: seit Monaten gebaut means built for months now.
The genitive shows possession and adds -es to short neuter nouns: des alten Hauses means of the old house.
Reported speech uses Konjunktiv I such as habe to flag a claim rather than a fact: sie habe den Unfall nicht verursacht.
Motion verbs form the perfect with sein, not haben: sind wir gewandert means we hiked.
Hose is singular in German though English pants is plural: eine bequeme Hose means one pair.
bevor is a subordinating word, so its verb moves to the end: bevor du das Haus betrittst.
